Alex: Ran an overnight nsys+perfetto capture against the 8-GPU regression. seeing a sharp latency cliff around step 78 when KV warmup transitions. attaching short trace excerpt.
Maria: Can you paste the nsys CLI and the perfetto window you used?
Alex: nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,nccl -o /tmp/ci/kv-warmup python run_profile.py --seq=2048 --batch=8
Alex: perfetto link (private): https://perfetto.link/abcd1234
Kevin: quick TL;DR from the trace: all-reduce waits on stream 7 for ~12ms at step 78, while kernel selection flips to an fp16 slower path. :eyes:
Natalie: that matches the KV handshake: a cache miss at step 77 produces a larger payload which bumps the kernel tiling heuristic into a different branch
Alex: short timeline excerpt:
```
[GPU0] kernel: attn_fwd_fp16 (1.9ms)
[GPU0] kernel: allreduce (12.3ms) nccl.coll:CU
[GPU1] kernel: attn_fwd_fp32 (3.8ms)
[GPU2] memcpy H2D (0.6ms)
```
Maria: can you also dump the KV warmup log? maybe the heuristic thinks there are more prefix tokens => different tiling decision
Alex: config snippet we used:
```
{"batching": {"max_batch": 64, "heuristic": "len_based", "kv_warmup_steps": 16}}
```
Kevin: hypothesis: len_based heuristic misclassifies because of skewed prefix length distribution; switching to `throughput_based` avoids the kernel flip and reduces the all-reduce serialization
Natalie: also saw NCCL trace showing serialized all-reduce starts offset by ~500us per rank starting at the cliff — that kills overlap and amplifies the 12ms window
Alex: next steps: run an isolated microbenchmark with controlled seq lengths + nvprof capture; try kv_warmup_steps=8 and flip heuristic; scheduling now
perfbot: scheduled job #4521 -> nsys/nvprof artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/perf/4521
Maria: perfect — if nvprof reproduces we can A/B the kernel selector threshold and ship a targeted fix to the runtime selector
Alex: will post results here once the job finishes. :thumbsup:
